panels.description:
This panel shows the rate of response sizes by resource and verb.

Outstandingly high values could give a hint for shoot operators on where
to start on the journey of reducing the load on the API servers,
by making sure to use WATCH requests instead of periodic LIST and
GET requests in the various controllers.

High values for WATCH requests could hint at reducing the rate of change for the specific resource.
panels.title: Response Size Rate Per Resource and Verb
Inflight Requests By Request Kind
panels.description: Instantaneous count of in-flight requests, split by mutating vs read-only. Shown as max_over_time to capture spikes within a scrape interval. With APF enabled, APF Seat Utilization is the primary saturation signal; use this panel to correlate with pre-APF baselines.

panels.title: Inqueue Requests By Request Kind
panels.description: Instantaneous count of requests waiting in APF queues, split by mutating vs read-only. Non-zero values indicate a priority level is saturated. Sustained queue depth precedes APF rejections.

panels.title: Request Terminations By Resource And Code
panels.description: Requests the API server forcibly terminated before completion, broken down by resource type and HTTP status code. A termination differs from a normal error response: the server initiated the disconnect (e.g. due to a timeout or APF deadline). Sustained high rates indicate overload or long-running requests being killed.

panels.title: ETCD Total Size
panels.description: Total etcd database size in bytes per endpoint. etcd performance degrades as the database grows. Watch for a sustained upward trend; compaction is automatic but can lag under heavy write loads.

panels.title: ETCD Object Counts By Resource
panels.description: Count of objects stored in etcd per resource type. Resource bloat (e.g. large numbers of ConfigMaps or Secrets) can cause slow LIST responses and increase etcd memory pressure.

panels.title: Total Storage Transformation Operations By Type And Prefix

panels.description: p$quantile admission latency broken down by admission step (VALIDATE, ADMIT, WEBHOOK). The WEBHOOK step reflects all admission webhooks collectively; use 'Duration Per Webhook' to identify which webhook is slow.
panels.title: Duration Per Step

panels.description: Panel shows how many watches are open (including the API Server's in-tree admission plug-ins).

targets.expr:
sum by (kind) (apiserver_registered_watchers{job=~"$job",pod=~"$pod",kind!=""})
  + on () group_left ()
    absent(apiserver_longrunning_requests) * 0
or
  sum by (resource) (apiserver_longrunning_requests{job=~"$job",pod=~"$pod",verb="WATCH"})

panels.title: Registered Watches Per Kind

panels.description: Counter of init events processed in watch cache.
panels.title: Init Event Count Per Resource

panels.description: Shows the watch event count per kind
panels.title: Event Count Per Kind

panels.description: Rate of watch-cache capacity increase events per resource. An increase event means the cache reflector detected it was too small and doubled its size. Frequent increases indicate heavy watch event volume for that resource.
panels.title: Cache Capacity Increases By Resource

panels.description: Rate of watch-cache capacity decrease events per resource. A decrease event means the cache was oversized and halved its allocation. Normal housekeeping; notable only if it immediately follows increases (thrashing).
panels.title: Cache Capacity Decreases By Resource

panels.description: 5xx error rate and 429 throttle rate as a percentage of total requests. 5xx indicates a server-side failure; 429 indicates intentional load shedding by APF. Streaming subresources are excluded from both.
panels.title: Error & Throttle Rate %

panels.description: Total number of kube-apiserver container restarts since the pod started.
panels.title: Restarts

panels.description: Total number of OOM kill events for the kube-apiserver container since the pod started.
panels.title: OOM Kills

panels.description: p99 read (LIST/GET) latency broken down by request scope. Kubernetes API SLO reference thresholds: cluster-scoped <40s, namespace-scoped <5s, resource-scoped <1s.
panels.title: Read Latency by Scope

panels.description: p99 write latency broken down by verb (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE). Kubernetes API SLO reference threshold: <1s. Divergence between verbs often points to a specific resource type or webhook.
panels.title: Write Latency by Verb

panels.description: p99 write latency broken down by resource type. Use alongside 'Write Latency p99 by Verb' to identify which resource is causing spikes. High latency on a specific resource often points to etcd key contention or a slow admission webhook on that resource.
panels.title: Write Latency by Resource

panels.description: APF seat capacity in use per priority level. Values approaching 100% mean requests will queue or be rejected before 5xx errors appear.
panels.title: APF Seat Utilization %

panels.description: Rate of requests rejected by APF per priority level and reason (queue-full, concurrency-limit, time-out).
panels.title: APF Rejections by Priority Level

panels.description: Time requests spend waiting in APF queues per priority level. Non-zero wait times indicate a priority level is saturated. Sustained wait times precede APF rejections and are an earlier warning signal than seat utilization alone.
panels.title: APF Queue Wait Latency

panels.description: 99th percentile latency of etcd calls from the kube-apiserver per operation. Elevated values indicate etcd is the bottleneck. Sustained p99 >500ms warrants investigating etcd health.
panels.title: etcd Round-Trip Latency

panels.description: Raw restart and OOM kill counters for each kube-apiserver pod. Each step up on the staircase is one event. An OOM kill step always coincides with a restart step; a restart step without a matching OOM step indicates a non-OOM cause (crash, rollout, etc.).
panels.title: Restart & OOM Kill History
